items.title: Finite-fuel meaning of a gradient-only proximal query

source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang; Samplinglib supplies finite-fuel semantics for the stated recurrence.

items.statement: Represent one gradient evaluation and residual test per positive-fuel step. With no fuel return none. Otherwise set z=y−eta g(x); on a successful test return the current x with count one, and on failure recurse from z with one less fuel, adding one to a successful count. This is a definition, not a correctness or termination theorem.
assumptions: E is a real normed vector space, g:E→E is an arbitrary oracle, eta and eps are real, y and x are points, and fuel is natural. Exact-real comparison is noncomputable. Source correctness assumptions apply in the separate execution theorem, not in this definition.

obligations.label: Finite-fuel construction with exact gradient-count and return convention

bindings.boundary: Construction only. No termination, minimizer, accuracy, expected cost or floating-point implementation claim; no query-list trace. The separate execution theorem proves successful fuel and its returned count.

assumption_deltas.source: The algorithm is applied to gradient V under curvature and positive-parameter assumptions.
assumption_deltas.lean: The recurrence is defined for arbitrary g, eta and eps in a real normed space.
assumption_deltas.reason: Only the construction is generalized. Its correctness theorem reinstates the source assumptions; the definition supplies no correctness conclusion.

assumption_deltas.source: Iterate until the first successful residual and return the current iterate.
assumption_deltas.lean: A natural-number fuel bounds the recursion; failure returns none and success records current point plus query count.
assumption_deltas.reason: Finite fuel gives a total Lean definition. The execution theorem supplies sufficient fuel; it does not turn this into a floating-point executable or an unbounded recursive program.
